target_customer: Freight carriers and truck makers that would pay for self-driving software for long-haul highway driving
problem: Long-haul trucking is expensive, driver supply is tight and highway driving is repetitive. Embark built autonomous driving software that takes over on highways and hands off for local driving.
business_model: Autonomous driving software licensed to trucking partners, with pilot runs on a fleet of company trucks

founders.name: Alex Rodrigues
previous_startups: Varden Labs (original name of Embark, campus self-driving shuttles)
founders.background_notes: The team entered YC with a different idea and pivoted to trucks.

founders.name: Brandon Moak
founders.background_notes: A third early co-founder named Michael is mentioned in a YC blog post but not identified further.

exit.reason: Embark ran out of money before reaching commercial production, cut about 70 percent of staff and retired its fleet of 24 trucks as part of the sale.

competitors.name: Otto (Uber)
competitors.what: Self-driving truck unit that completed a 120 mile Budweiser delivery in Colorado in October 2016

technical_complexity.rationale: Safe self-driving on public highways with heavy trucks needs perception, planning and safety validation at research grade, and hardware integration with trucks.

defensibility.rationale: Years of road data and engineering are hard to copy, but several well funded rivals and large trucking players were pursuing the same goal and no one had a clear lead.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large players were already building autonomous trucks in 2016 and 2017. Embark outlasted Otto but ran out of money and sold for a fraction of its SPAC valuation.

market_need_then: Trucking faced a driver shortage and high labor cost, and the 2016 Otto demonstration showed investor and customer interest in autonomous freight.

branding.name_origin: The company began as Varden Labs and changed its name to Embark; no source gives the reason for the new name.
branding.domain_note: Used embarktrucks.com, which now returns a 404 after the acquisition.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical and milestone focused, such as first coast-to-coast autonomous drive

branding.brand_signature: Claim of the first autonomous coast-to-coast truck drive

rebrands.why: Pivot from campus self-driving shuttles to trucks; reason for the name not sourced.

branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage around the 2021 SPAC listing and a YC blog post on the road to IPO; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Known in autonomous vehicle and trucking circles through press and the public listing, but a generic word name with no evidence that brand drove growth.

pivots.from: Self-driving shuttles for campuses as Varden Labs
pivots.why: Move to a larger freight market; stated in YC blog that the team came into YC planning shuttles.

outcome_analysis: Embark pivoted from campus shuttles to autonomous trucking and went public in November 2021 through a SPAC deal first valued at about 5.2 billion dollars. Heavy redemptions cut the cash raised, and the company ran out of money before commercial production. It cut about 70 percent of its staff and was bought by Applied Intuition in May 2023 for about 71 million dollars, so autonomous freight proved earlier and more capital hungry than the SPAC story assumed.
notes: Directory status is Public, but Embark was acquired by Applied Intuition in 2023 and went private, so exit type is acquisition. Pre-SPAC rounds (reported Series B of 70 million, Series C of 30 million and total over 117 million) were not confirmed by a second source, so only the SPAC PIPE is recorded. The SPAC closed in November 2021 with a trust of about 314 million remaining after redemptions. One aggregator claims a shutdown in March 2023, which conflicts with the acquisition coverage. Competitors Starsky Robotics, Peloton and TuSimple were found only in 2018 or undated sources, so they are omitted from the founding list. Founding year given as 2016 or 2018 in different sources.
